## 2. Pattern observation (significant finding for triage)

The matrix reveals a **highly consistent authoring convention** across the entire codebase that was not anticipated by the plan's "Initial diagnostic shows variance" framing:

### 2.1 The "I1–I4 active, I5–I10 inherited" pattern

**Only 2 of the 18 chapters carry full 10/10 coverage in any scenario:**
- **Genesis 1** (all 4 scenarios at 10/10) — the **canonical OT period anchor**
- **John 1** (both scenarios at 10/10) — the **canonical NT period anchor**

**All 16 other chapters** populate ONLY I1 Political, I2 Economy, I3 Daily Life, and (sometimes) I4 Social Structure. Categories I5 Education, I6 Military, I7 Arts, I8 Science, I9 Religion, I10 Neighboring peoples are uniformly absent across all 16 chapters × all scenarios. This is not random scatter — it is a single binary pattern with 100% rule consistency.

### 2.2 The cross-reference convention is partially documented

- **NT chapters (5 of 5 non-anchor):** John 2, John 3, Matthew 1, Matthew 2, Matthew 3 all open Section I with an explicit `> **Cross-reference:**` quote-block pointing to John 1 as the canonical period anchor. The convention is **EXPLICITLY DOCUMENTED** in each chapter.
- **Genesis chapters (11 of 11 non-anchor):** Genesis 2–12 implement the same I1–I4-only authoring pattern but contain **NO** equivalent cross-reference quote-block pointing to Genesis 1. The convention is **IMPLICIT but UNDOCUMENTED** for OT chapters.

This is a structural inconsistency at the codebase level — the same authoring convention applied with different levels of reader-facing documentation.

### 2.3 Interpretation

The pattern strongly suggests one of two original-authoring intents (which Phase 0 / Phase 6.6G / Phase 7 editorial logs may or may not record):

- **Interpretation A (anchor convention):** The chapter at the start of each book (Gen 1, John 1) was authored as a canonical period-anchor with full 10/10 × all-scenarios coverage; subsequent chapters in the same book were authored to ONLY add categories whose context genuinely differs chapter-to-chapter (typically political/economic/daily-life shifts driven by narrative events). Categories I5–I10 are inherited from the anchor unless explicitly contradicted.

- **Interpretation B (incomplete authoring):** The chapter at the start of each book was authored to completion as a template; later chapters were truncated to a minimum-viable-product pattern with the intention to fill them in later but the work was never done. Under this reading, 16 × ~5–6 missing categories = ~80–96 (i) Genuine gaps that need authoring.

The presence of the explicit cross-reference quote-block in the 5 NT chapters strongly favors **Interpretation A** for those chapters. The absence of an equivalent quote-block in Genesis 2–12 leaves Interpretation A vs. B ambiguous for OT chapters — pending project-lead confirmation, but the structural symmetry with NT suggests A.

## 3. Initial triage proposal (step 8.2 — pending project-lead confirmation)

If **Interpretation A** is correct for all chapters:

| Cell class | Count | Triage |
|------------|-------|--------|
| `✓` cells | 220 | Already complete — no action |
| `–` cells in NT chapters with `[xref→J1]` (default-(iii) per §4.0 plan, audit §3.2) | 90 | **(iii) Implicit coverage** — already documented via explicit cross-reference; no action |
| `–` cells in Genesis 2–12 (parallel pattern, undocumented) | 290 | **Either (iii) Implicit coverage with the gap being lack-of-documentation, OR (i) Genuine gap depending on Interpretation A vs. B** — see §3.1 |

The **dominant Phase 8 work product under Interpretation A** is NOT authoring 290 new I-N entries across Genesis 2–12. It is **adding the cross-reference quote-block** to Genesis 2–12 (11 chapter files × 4 locales = 44 files) to bring OT chapters into structural parity with NT chapters. The actual category coverage stays identical — but the reader-facing documentation becomes consistent.

If **Interpretation B** is correct, the Phase 8 work product is closer to the original 60–120h Maximal estimate from the plan's Q1.

### 3.1 What counts as a "narrative-specific genuine gap" requiring (i) backfill?

Per audit §5.5 refinement (directly-period-relevant filter), even under Interpretation A there may be a small number of (i) gaps where a category absent from the anchor cannot adequately cover the chapter's narrative-specific context. Examples (preliminary; subject to step 8.2 manual review):

- **John 2 I2 Economy:** John 1's I2 covers generic Galilean economy; John 2's stone-vessel industry + temple-commerce confrontation may warrant a chapter-specific I2 augmentation. **Already present** (`✓` in matrix) — this is the convention working correctly.
- **Matthew 2 I10 Neighboring peoples:** John 1's I10 covers Roman/Greek/Parthian neighbors generically; Matthew 2's Persian/Parthian Magi narrative + Egyptian refuge corridor may warrant a chapter-specific I10. **Currently absent.** Candidate for (i) Genuine gap.
- **Genesis 9 I9 Religion:** Genesis 1's I9 covers Mesopotamian creation cosmology; Genesis 9's Noachic covenant + animal-blood-prohibition may warrant a chapter-specific I9 covering ANE flood-aftermath religion + bloodless-altar practice. **Currently absent.** Candidate for (i) Genuine gap.

The actual list of (i)-classified cells after manual triage is likely **small** (estimate: 10–30 cells across all 18 chapters), not the 380 raw absences.

## 4. Updated Phase 8 effort estimate (post-diagnostic)

The original plan §6 Q1 estimates need to be revised given the pattern observation:

- **Option A (Maximal — every (i) cell across all chapters):** Drops from 60–120h to ~10–25h IF Interpretation A is confirmed. The dominant work is adding cross-reference quote-blocks to 11 Genesis chapters × 4 locales = 44 files (~3–5h) + authoring ~10–30 narrative-specific (i) backfill entries across 4 locales (~7–20h).
- **Option B (Canary + propagation):** ~8–15h unchanged.
- **Option C (Scenario-priority — only Scenario A across chapters):** Drops from 25–40h to ~8–15h.

**Strong shift in recommendation:** if Interpretation A is correct, **Option A (Maximal) is suddenly cheap** — and yields full codebase-wide consistency in one phase rather than a canary + propagation chain. This was not visible until the diagnostic landed.

## 5. Project-lead decision input (for step 8.3)

The diagnostic surfaces 4 questions the project lead needs to answer before step 8.4 execution begins:

### Q-INTERP (NEW, takes precedence over original Q1/Q4)
**Confirm Interpretation A (anchor + cross-reference convention) or Interpretation B (incomplete authoring)?**

The matrix pattern + the existing NT explicit cross-reference + the structural symmetry between Gen 1 → Gen 2–12 and John 1 → John 2/3 + Matt 1/2/3 strongly favor A. But A vs. B is ultimately a Phase 0 / Phase 6.6 authoring-intent question that the project lead can confirm authoritatively. The phase plan must hinge on this.

If A is confirmed:
- **Phase 8 dominant work product:** add cross-reference quote-block to Genesis 2–12 + author the 10–30 narrative-specific (i) backfill cells; estimated ~10–25h total across 4 locales (Option A Maximal feasible in this phase).

If B is confirmed:
- **Phase 8 dominant work product:** author the 290 absences across Genesis 2–12 + the 90 absences across NT chapters (after the cross-reference quote-blocks are ignored as not-sufficient documentation); estimated ~60–120h. Option A Maximal is back to the originally-estimated burden; Option B canary is the safer alternative.

### Q1 (unchanged in form, materially affected by Q-INTERP)
Backfill scope: Option A / B / C — answer depends on Q-INTERP.

### Q2 (unchanged)
Heading-form heterogeneity: leave as-is (recommended).

### Q3 (unchanged)
Per-chapter scenario-count audit: no (recommended).

### Q4 (canary chapter, only if Q1 = Option B)
**Updated recommendation post-diagnostic:** Genesis 9 (no cross-reference convention to navigate; substantive narrative-specific candidates for I7 Arts/Literature on flood-narrative parallels + I9 Religion on Noachic covenant + I10 Neighboring peoples on post-flood ethnogeography). Genesis 12 (Avraham's call to Canaan) is the alternate — also no cross-reference; Early Bronze Age period context anchor.

## 6. Step 8.2 next action

Pending Q-INTERP answer, step 8.2 produces the formal (i) / (ii) / (iii) classification of every `–` cell. The classification is largely mechanical once Q-INTERP is decided:

- **Under Interpretation A:** all `–` cells in Genesis 2–12 are (iii) Implicit coverage (cross-reference convention applies — currently undocumented in OT). All `–` cells in NT chapters with `[xref→J1]` are (iii). A small subset of cells (estimate 10–30) are (i) Genuine gap based on chapter-narrative-specificity.
- **Under Interpretation B:** all 380 `–` cells are (i) Genuine gap pending case-by-case review.

The manual triage at step 8.2 then refines this default to identify the specific (i) cells under either interpretation, and produces the editorial-absence notes for any cells classified as (ii).

**Diagnostic complete.** Step 8.2 (triage) is automated under Interpretation A; substantive under Interpretation B. Step 8.3 project-lead decision required before step 8.4 execution can begin. The Q-INTERP question is the critical pre-execution gate.
